visa_on_arrival.description: Ghana offers visa on arrival for citizens of all African Union member states and some other countries

e_visa.description: Electronic visa available for most nationalities

providers.name: Vodafone Ghana
providers.coverage: Good urban and major highway coverage

providers.name: AirtelTigo
providers.coverage: Growing network, good in major cities

general_info.airport_availability: Yes, all 3 providers at Kotoka International Airport
general_info.mobile_money: All providers offer mobile money services (MTN MoMo, Vodafone Cash, AirtelTigo Money)

exchange_rate_approximation.note: Rates fluctuate daily. Check current rates at banks or forex bureaus

atms.availability: Widely available in cities, limited in rural areas
atms.fees: Varies by bank; expect GHS 5-15 per transaction
tips: Use ATMs inside banks for security
Carry some cash for rural areas

payment_methods.cards: Accepted in hotels, large restaurants, supermarkets in cities
payment_methods.mobile_money: Very popular; MTN MoMo most widely accepted
payment_methods.recommended: Carry mix of cash and cards; small denominations useful

general_safety.crime_level: Moderate; Ghana is one of the safest countries in West Africa
recommendations: Keep valuables secure and out of sight
Use hotel safes for passports and extra cash
Be cautious in crowded markets and busy areas
Avoid displaying expensive jewelry or electronics
Use registered taxis or ride-sharing apps (Uber, Bolt, Yango)
Don't walk alone at night in unfamiliar areas
Keep copies of important documents separately

vaccinations_required: Yellow fever (mandatory; proof required at entry)
malaria_prevention: Wear long sleeves and pants in evenings
health_safety.water_safety: Drink only bottled or filtered water; avoid ice unless from trusted sources
food_safety: Avoid street food if you have a sensitive stomach

medical_facilities.general: Private hospitals offer better service; bring travel insurance

road_safety.conditions: Variable; major highways good, rural roads can be poor
tips: Avoid driving at night outside cities
Watch for pedestrians and animals on roads
Consider hiring a driver for long trips

scams_to_avoid.warning: Too good to be true offers; avoid engaging

scams_to_avoid.prevention: Agree on price before entering; use ride-sharing apps
Use licensed guides; book through reputable agencies

seasons.name: Dry Season
seasons.characteristics: Low humidity, little rain, hot and dusty (especially January-February)

seasons.name: Rainy Season (Major)
seasons.characteristics: Heavy rains, high humidity, lush greenery

seasons.name: Rainy Season (Minor)
seasons.characteristics: Lighter rains compared to major season

temperature.northern: Higher temperatures, can exceed 40°C (104°F) in dry season

greetings.description: Greetings are very important in Ghanaian culture
tips: Always greet people before starting a conversation
Handshakes are common; use right hand
Ask 'How are you?' and expect same in return
Elders should be greeted first and with respect

dress_code.beaches: Modest swimwear; topless bathing not acceptable
dress_code.religious_sites: Cover shoulders and knees; remove shoes
dress_code.note: Ghanaians dress well; overly casual may be seen as disrespectful

rules: Always ask permission before photographing people
Offer to share photos with locals if they're interested

tipping.taxis: Round up fare or add GHS 2-5

gestures.left_hand: Avoid using left hand for giving/receiving items; considered impolite
gestures.pointing: Use whole hand, not one finger
gestures.beckoning: Wave with palm down, not palm up

metadata.source: Ghana Tourism Authority, Ghana Immigration Service, compiled by AI Labs Africa
metadata.disclaimer: Information subject to change; verify current requirements before travel
